overview: Written quality was variable; many marks were lost through imprecise definitions and not answering the question actually set.
Stronger candidates reasoned clearly, set out calculations logically, planned Level of Response answers and applied ideas to unfamiliar contexts.
Weaker candidates struggled with powers of ten, unit prefixes and cross-sectional area, and set out unstructured calculations poorly.
In 'show' questions the method must be explicit, with the unknown as the subject; using the given value to work backwards earns no credit.
Write inside the answer spaces since scripts are scanned, and keep handwriting legible.
assessment_for_learning: Underline key terms in the question stem (e.g. 'deceleration is constant').
Plot graphs with a sharp pencil and draw best-fit lines with a clear 30 cm ruler; thick points and lines lose marks.
Practise matching a graph's axes to y = mx + c to identify what the gradient and intercept represent.
Be able to describe light-gate methods for velocity and acceleration, including connection to a timer or data logger.
Practise writing structured explanations of phenomena for Level of Response questions.
If you quote an equation as a definition, define every symbol.
